episode_title: ENCORE: How to Perform Under Pressure Aligned with Your Goals

real_qa.q: How did Wild Coffee Marketing transition from tactical digital work to offering strategy-led CMO services?
real_qa.r: Amy realized that companies were doing marketing work absent of strategy, purely tactical and not cohesive with operational and revenue goals. She and her business partner decided to shift the model to provide a strategy layer first: they now insist on a strategy workshop and roadmap before starting any engagement, positioning Wild Coffee as an outsourced CMO that CEOs need but don't require full-time.
real_qa.requete: Wild Coffee Marketing strategy CMO services

real_qa.q: What are the key KPI metrics that Wild Coffee Marketing uses to measure client engagement success?
real_qa.r: Amy believes every client engagement needs no more than five KPIs, though they may track up to 10. Top line revenue is always a consideration. These five KPIs per engagement are aligned with clients at the beginning and tracked on a weekly, monthly, and quarterly basis to ensure accountability and measurable progress toward business objectives.
real_qa.requete: Wild Coffee Marketing KPIs client engagement

real_qa.q: How does Wild Coffee Marketing maintain team accountability and culture in a fully distributed workforce?
real_qa.r: The company uses EOS (Entrepreneurial Operating System) as its operating system, which creates a cadence of meetings and sessions for ideation, discussion, and planning. Every 90 days, Amy conducts quarterly reviews asking team members to rate their energy level on a scale of one to ten. The culture emphasizes on-camera meetings for connection, clarity breaks, no back-to-back scheduling on certain days, and no client emails on weekends.

real_qa.q: What scheduling practices does Wild Coffee Marketing use to improve meeting punctuality and mental clarity?
real_qa.r: Amy schedules all client meetings and facilitated sessions on the quarter hour—either a quarter after or a quarter till—to give people time to finish their previous meeting and be fully present. Friday afternoons are protected from meetings unless absolutely necessary. The company also avoids early Monday meetings, with more openings Thursday and Friday, recognizing natural circadian rhythms and a bell curve to the work week.
real_qa.requete: quarter hour scheduling meeting punctuality culture

real_qa.q: What specific market challenge did Wild Coffee Marketing address for a client in the wedding industry?
real_qa.r: One client believed the industry as a whole was 30% off that year. Wild Coffee worked with them to pivot their wedding segment strategy in response to inflation-based economy pressures where fewer brides and grooms were having formal weddings, compounded by a major bridal retailer laying off staff. This required real-time strategic adjustment rather than generic junior marketing responses.

real_qa.q: How did Amy Anderson's accidental entrepreneurship journey reshape her leadership priorities?
real_qa.r: Amy started consulting out of need rather than intention after an unexpected divorce with two young children, seeking flexibility to be present for them. Her parents gave her 12 months and $12,000 to become self-sustaining. Over almost 10 years, her priorities shifted from pure survival and understanding her business model to creating high-performance teams, building a culture of accountability, and designing the best workplace where people learn, grow, and choose to stay rather than leave.

guest.bio_context: Amy Anderson has more than 30 years of experience in marketing across major brands including Calvin Klein, 17 Magazine, and New York Times Digital. She transitioned from corporate marketing to entrepreneurship after an unexpected divorce, initially starting as a consultant before co-founding Wild Coffee Marketing in 2017 with a business partner. Her focus evolved from survival-mode consulting to building high-performance teams and providing strategy-led outsourced CMO services to scaling businesses.
